1class BinaryTree:
2    def __init__(self):
3        self.array = []
4
5    # calculate the index of a node's parent
6    def parent(self, index):
7        return (index - 1) // 2
8
9    # calculate the index of a node's left child
10    def left_child(self, index):
11        return 2 * index + 1
12
13    # calculate the index of a node's right child
14    def right_child(self, index):
15        return 2 * index + 2
16
17    # check if a node at a given index has a parent
18    def has_parent(self, index):
19        return self.parent(index) >= 0
20
21    # check if a node at a given index has a left child
22    def has_left_child(self, index):
23        return self.left_child(index) < len(self.array)
24
25    # check if a node at a given index has a right child
26    def has_right_child(self, index):
27        return self.right_child(index) < len(self.array)
28
29    # add a new element to the binary tree 
30    # for demonstration purposes
31    def insert(self, value):
32        self.array.append(value)
33
34    # print the tree contents (for demonstration)
35    def print_tree(self):
36        print(self.array)
37
38
39bt = BinaryTree()
40
41# insert elements into the binary tree
42for i in range(10):
43        bt.insert(i)
44
45# display binary tree
46bt.print_tree()
47print()
48
49# check some relationships
50index = 3
51if bt.has_parent(index):
52    print(f"Parent of node at index {index}: {bt.array[bt.parent(index)]}")
53    
54if bt.has_left_child(index):
55    print(f"Left child of node at index {index}: {bt.array[bt.left_child(index)]}")
56    
57if bt.has_right_child(index):
58        print(f"Right child of node at index {index}: {bt.array[bt.right_child(index)]}")
